headline: High-risk shared-workspace and output-trust paths: Dify can write broad server-side state while MinerU exposes MCP/API document processing, creating medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can write filesystem and uses tools wired into agent/workflow flows; MinerU exposes MCP Server and API surfaces for document processing. If MinerU outputs are fed into Dify workflows or shared storage, attacker-controlled document text can become instructions. The shared channel is plausible, but not proven by docs, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs are ingested by Dify workflows or knowledge-base files
IF document text from MinerU is treated as trusted instructions by Dify
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of MinerU outputs into Dify prompts
Add a provenance tag to all MinerU-derived text
Require manual review before workflow execution
Restrict Dify tools to allowlisted actions only

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge-base content and conversation logs and can write/read filesystem; MinerU processes PDFs, DOCX, XLSX, OCR text, and exposes MCP/API surfaces. If they share a workspace or Dify ingests MinerU outputs, sensitive document content can flow into Dify logs or model-provider calls. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default deployments, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF MinerU processes sensitive documents that Dify later stores in conversation logs
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared workspace or upload directory
mitigations: Separate storage locations for each agent
Turn off or minimize Dify conversation logging
Redact sensitive fields before passing MinerU output onward
Use per-agent credentials and access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify has broad filesystem write and server-side subprocess execution, while MinerU is multi-threaded and exposes MCP/API interfaces. They do not both advertise unrestricted write to the same directory, but shared state via Dify datastore and overlapping file/workflow surfaces create a realistic conflict path. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared directory or datastore
IF concurrent runs target the same document set without locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue
Disable concurrent mutation of shared artifacts
Use read-only mounts for MinerU inputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can orchestrate tools and workflows, so MinerU extraction results may be consumed as authoritative downstream inputs. MinerU is a document parser, not a verifier, and Dify can act on workflow outputs. That creates a default path where extraction errors or hallucinated OCR text propagate into later actions; the blast radius is multiple work products, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Dify uses MinerU output as a source of truth without validation
IF downstream workflow steps trigger actions based on extracted text
mitigations: Insert a validation step before any action-taking workflow
Require human approval for extracted facts
Compare MinerU output against the source document for critical fields
Limit downstream automation to non-destructive actions

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, but Dify explicitly handles model-provider API keys, tool credentials, knowledge-base content, and conversation logs, while MinerU is documented as private/fully offline. The main compliance issue is a potential retention/logging mismatch if the pair processes regulated documents; no specific residency or certification conflict is documented, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through Dify conversation logs
IF retention settings differ between Dify storage and MinerU local outputs
mitigations: Set explicit retention limits in Dify
Keep regulated documents out of conversation logs
Store MinerU outputs in a separate compliant repository
Document deletion/export procedures for both systems
